Notebook introduction

This document provides an exhaustive, bit-by-bit technical breakdown of the **Scene Graph Subsystem** in the Retiam WebGPU Engine. It covers the node hierarchy ([`Entity.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts)), the top-level composition coordinator ([`SceneComposer.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/SceneComposer.ts)), unified 256-byte aligned GPU state memory blocks ([`State.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/State.ts)), hierarchical matrix propagation, version memoization, and zero-allocation render queue generation.
1. High-Level Architectural Overview
Retiam couples a flexible **Hierarchical Scene Graph** with an **Entity-Component-System (ECS)** and a **Zero-GC Bindless GPU Memory Pipeline**:

    subgraph "2. SceneComposer Hierarchical Traversal (Zero-GC)"
        Traverse["SceneComposer.traverse()"] --> HierarchyMemo["Version Memoization Check (Local & Parent Transform Flags)"]
        HierarchyMemo --> MatMult["World Matrix Evaluation: M_world = M_parent * M_local"]
        MatMult --> StateAlloc["Direct State Allocation in GlobalStateAllocator"]
        StateAlloc --> ScissorCalc["Hardware Scissor Box & AABB Intersection"]
        ScissorCalc --> RenderQueue["Sorted RenderQueue Insertion (ndcZ + zIndex)"]
    end

    subgraph "3. GPU Memory Synchronization"
        RenderQueue --> StateManager["StateDataManager (Contiguous CPU cpuData Mirror)"]
        StateManager --> SingleUpload["Single queue.writeBuffer Upload"]
        SingleUpload --> GlobalStorage["@group(2) @binding(0) Global State Buffer (EntityState[])"]
    end

blocks.text: 3. The Unified 256-Byte Aligned State Memory Block ([State.ts](../src/engine/core/State.ts))

To eliminate per-entity uniform buffer allocation overhead, Retiam packs all transformation, 2D vector styling, and 3D PBR material properties into a **single 256-byte aligned contiguous Float32 memory block**:
Each entity state occupies 64 floats (256 bytes). The sub-buffers share one `Float32Array` slice:

cells: `fill: vec4f`; `stroke: vec4f`; stroke width, opacity, z-index, cap, joint, set mask and padding
World `_matrix: mat4x4f`; `_offset: vec4f`; `_t1`, `_t2`; `_bit_mask: u32` and padding
`color: vec4f`; `emissive: vec4f` (RGB + strength); roughness, metallic, transmission, IOR; albedo / normal textures and padding

blocks.text: 4. Scene Graph Traversal & Render Queue Building ([SceneComposer.ts](../src/engine/core/SceneComposer.ts))

The [`SceneComposer`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/SceneComposer.ts) orchestrates the execution loop and converts the active entity tree into a flat, depth-sorted `render_queue` every frame.

blocks.text: Key Performance Innovations:

children: State instances for non-rendering container nodes are recycled from pre-allocated pools (`this.statePool[this.statePoolIndex++]`).
Render command descriptors are recycled from `this.renderCommandPool`.
Traversal automatically increments `this.z_index += this.delta`, guaranteeing consistent visual layer ordering without requiring manual $z$-index management.
When an entity sets `scissorClipRect`, the engine transforms the rectangle into screen-space pixels and clips all nested child nodes automatically.

7. Performance Best Practices

children: Structural nodes that only provide parent transforms should use `new Group()`. They do not allocate render queue entries or GPU draw calls.

Keep hierarchies reasonably balanced. Retiam's transform caching skips matrix re-multiplication if `UPDATE_FLAG` is `false`, ensuring rapid sub-millisecond traversal even for scenes with 50,000+ entities.
Setting `entity.VISIBILITY = false` or `entity.paint.opacity = 0` completely culls the entity and all of its nested children from traversal, render queue building, and state buffer upload.
